g.text: host_tcd_rx_buffer — how banks and slots fill on each wr_clk edge
Assume reset is released, all slots are free, frame_valid=1 and write_fire=1 on every rising edge.
Defaults: SLOT_SAMPLES=1024, SLOT_COUNT=4, ROWS=128. Frame n carries {Dn, Cn, Bn, An}.

div.div:
At edge E[n]: register the incoming frame's data/address/enable, AND commit the frame registered at E[n−1].
The RAM columns below show writes committed at that edge. A/B/C/D commits always happen together.

g.text: E[8]: slot 0, RAM row 0 is complete in every bank: lanes 0–7 contain samples 0–7.
E[1024]: the last sample of slot 0 commits in every bank. The next frame is already registered for slot 1.
State immediately AFTER E[1025] — all banks have the same occupancy

g.text: Next: slot 1 fills, then slot 2, then slot 3. After slot 3, wr_slot wraps to slot 0 only as an index;
writing can resume there only when ownership has released slot 0. Otherwise frames are dropped for all four banks.
Frame numbers are example sample indices, not reset-relative clock counts or timestamps. Any pause in write_fire changes this timeline.
